preamble: The dominant description of Standard Bulgarian vowel reduction (Tilkov & Boyadzhiev 1977) has the central vowels /a/ and /ɤ/ (ъ) neutralize in unstressed syllables as [ɐ]: the stressed ъ of мъж [mɤʃ] 'man' is [ɐ] in мъже [mɐˈʒɛ] 'men', and Ternes & Vladimirova-Buhtz (1990) transcribe unstressed ъ as [ɐ] (пътникът [ˈpɤtnikɐt]). Acoustic studies (Andreeva, Barry & Koreman 2013; Dokovova et al. 2019) find unstressed /ɤ/ raised rather than lowered and unstressed /a/ moving toward it, so the lowering half of the neutralization is disputed.

examples.from: пътникът 'the traveller', unstressed article -ът (cf. stressed мъжъ̀т [mɐˈʒɤt])
examples.note: The definite article -ът is [ɤt] under stress and [ɐt] unstressed.

sources: Ternes, E., & Vladimirova-Buhtz, T. (1990). Bulgarian. Journal of the International Phonetic Association 20(1), 45–47. https://doi.org/10.1017/S0025100300004072
